paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: wisdom isn't just knowing stuff, it's the way you live. Solomon keeps setting two roads side by side all through this chapter, and the road you walk decides where you end up. The one that tops them all is this: "The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life, turning a man from the snares of death." (Proverbs 14:27)

So how do you tell the roads apart? Solomon says "There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death." (Proverbs 14:12) I think that verse should make all of us pause, because feeling sure is not the same as being right. The wise man "watches his steps" (Proverbs 14:15), and he starts by fearing the LORD, which is why the upright man in Proverbs 14:2 is the one who fears Him. That fear isn't a cold fear, either, because "He who fears the LORD is secure in confidence, and his children shall have a place of refuge." (Proverbs 14:26)

Then Solomon shows what the wise road looks like on a Tuesday. It's honest words, real work instead of "mere talk," patience instead of a short fuse, and kindness to the poor, since "whoever is kind to the needy honors Him." (Proverbs 14:31) Even "a tranquil heart is life to the body, but envy rots the bones." (Proverbs 14:30) So, baker, don't just trust the way that feels right today. Ask the LORD to teach you His way, and drink from that fountain.
